title: Installation
text: setupmjr is distributed as a compiled Go CLI binary. Install it via system package managers, release installers, or from source. Optional R and Python wrappers dispatch to the installed setupmjr binary.

title: Installation
text:
Release asset matrix
GitHub Releases publish Go CLI binaries for:

Linux (amd64, arm64) as .tar.gz
macOS (amd64, arm64) as .tar.gz
Windows (amd64, arm64) as .zip (plus .exe bare binaries for installer scripts)
Stable direct-download bare binaries for installer scripts:

setupmjr_linux_<arch>
setupmjr_darwin_<arch>
setupmjr_windows_<arch>.exe


Python and R components are wrappers around the same CLI and are platform-neutral. Install the wrapper package (pip/R) and ensure setupmjr is installed on PATH.

title: Installation
text:
Ubuntu / Debian

Option 1: Local Release Installer (No sudo required)
Install the latest release binary into the first writable directory already present in your PATH:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
bash install-local.sh
If no writable path entry exists, the installer will stop with guidance.
To uninstall:
bash uninstall-local.sh


Option 2: Install from APT Repository (Recommended for automatic updates, but requires sudo)






Warning



The APT repository is an upcoming feature and not yet fully configured.


Install and keep setupmjr up to date directly via apt:
# Install prerequisites
sudo apt-get install -y curl gpg

# Add repository signing key
curl -fsSL https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo/KEY.gpg \
   | sudo gpg --dearmor -o /usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg

# Add apt source
echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/apt-miguelrodo.gpg] https://miguelrodo.github.io/apt-miguelrodo stable main" \
   | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/apt-miguelrodo.list >/dev/null

# Install setupmjr
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y setupmjr
To uninstall:
sudo apt-get remove setupmjr


Option 3: System-wide from Release .deb (requires sudo)
Prefer Option 1 (APT) for automatic updates. If needed, manually download and install a release .deb from the Releases page:
VERSION_SETUPMJR=1.2.6
ARCH="$(dpkg --print-architecture)"
wget "https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/releases/download/v${VERSION_SETUPMJR}/setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"
sudo dpkg -i "setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"
rm "setupmjr_${VERSION_SETUPMJR}_${ARCH}.deb"

# Fix any dependency issues
sudo apt-get install -f
To uninstall:
sudo dpkg -r setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
Windows

Option 1: Installer Script
Download and install the pre-compiled setupmjr.exe into the first writable directory already present in your PATH:

Clone the repository:
git clone https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git
cd setupmjr
Run the installer:
.\install.ps1

The installer downloads the latest setupmjr.exe binary from GitHub releases and places it in the first writable directory in your current PATH.
Requirements: PowerShell and network access to GitHub releases.
(Note: Ensure you are executing this within a PowerShell console pwsh or powershell.exe, as native cmd.exe will not interpret the script correctly.)
To uninstall:
.\install.ps1 -Uninstall


Option 2: Scoop
scoop bucket add setupmjr https://github.com/MiguelRodo/scoop-bucket
scoop install setupmjr

title: Installation
text:
From Source (Go)
Requires the Go toolchain installed.
Install directly from the remote module path:
go install github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/cmd/setupmjr@latest
Or build from a local clone (Linux-specific example shown):
git clone [https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git](https://github.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr.git)
cd setupmjr
go build -o setupmjr ./cmd/setupmjr
# Install system-wide on Linux/macOS
sudo mv setupmjr /usr/local/bin/

title: hpc
text:
Installation
Assuming that the HPC is running on Linux, the following line will install setupmjr without requiring sudo permission:
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MiguelRodo/setupmjr/main/install-local.sh | bash
Confirm that installation worked by running:
setupmjr --version
If the above does not work, then setupmjr may not be on your system PATH. In that case, you can add the following line to your shell profile (typically ~/.bashrc):
export PATH="$HOME/.local/bin:$PATH"
Then run:
source ~/.bashrc
At this point, the following should succeed:
setupmjr --version
If not, then the initial installation failed.

title: hpc
text:
Setup
The following command will configure the HPC environment:
setupmjr hpc
Apart from needing to edit one file for Git authentication if this has not been setup yet (see below), this command requires no other user input.
setupmjr hpc does the following:

Helps store large files effectively: Large files are stored in the /scratch space (if available) rather than /home, to respect HPC storage policies.
Authenticates with Git: Scripts are added to which the user needs to simply add their GitHub username and a personal access token (PAT) to enable seamless Git operations from the HPC environment.
Add Apptainer and SLURM helpers: If these tools are available on the HPC, helper scripts will be added to simplify their usage.
Configures radian: If you use radian as your R terminal, it is configured to work properly on the HPC.

Each of these features can be configured independently via the respective subcommands (hpc scratch, hpc apptainer, hpc slurm, hpc git, hpc r).

Setting up Git
To work with Git, you need to do two things:

Supply Git with your name and email (if not already configured).
Provide Git with credentials to authenticate with remote repositories, e.g. GitHub.

To set this up, run the following command (which is also part of the setupmjr hpc command):
setupmjr hpc git
You will be prompted to enter your full name and email address (if these are not already set), which Git uses to identify you as the author of commits.
In addition, you will be prompted to enter your GitHub username and a personal access token (PAT). This allows Git to authenticate with GitHub when you push commits or perform other operations that require authentication.
To get a GitHub PAT, go to your GitHub account settings, navigate to “Developer settings” > “Personal access tokens”, and generate a new token with the appropriate scopes (e.g. repo for full control of private repositories).
If you skip entering any of the above information, you can always run setupmjr hpc git again to set it up later.

title: hpc
text:
Details
Git authentication is configured by the following:

It is ensured that .bashrc.d files are sourced by .bashrc.
The credential helper is set to the following:
!f() { sleep 1; echo "username=${GITHUB_USER:-TOKEN}"; echo "password=${GH_TOKEN:-$GITHUB_TOKEN}"; }; f
A script is added to ~/.bashrc.d/login.sh, which has space for the user to add their GitHub username and PAT, and then exports these as environment variables (GITHUB_USER and GITHUB_USERNAME for the user name and GITHUB_TOKEN, GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_PAT for the token).

title: hpc
text:
Details
The hpc scratch command configures the environment to use the /scratch directory by doing the following:

It ensures that .bashrc.d files are sourced by .bashrc.
A script is added to ~/.bashrc.d/hpc-scratch.sh, which explicitly exports paths for Apptainer, Singularity, renv, and R libraries to use /scratch/$USER. Specifically, it sets the following environment variables:

RENV_CONFIG_PAK_ENABLED=false
RENV_CONFIG_SANDBOX_ENABLED=false
RENV_PATHS_LIBRARY_ROOT=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R/library
RENV_PATHS_CACHE=/scratch/${USER}/renv/cache:/renv/cache
RENV_PATHS_ROOT=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R/library
R_LIBS=/scratch/${USER}/.local/lib/R

title: hpc
text:
Details
The hpc slurm command sets up these tools by doing the following:

It ensures that ~/.local/bin is added to your system’s PATH environment variable by (if required) adding an export statement to your .bashrc.
It places the specific utility wrapper scripts (slurm-sbatch, slurm-sintx, slurm-squeue) directly into ~/.local/bin/.

title: hpc
text:
Details
The ~/.radian_profile file is created if it does not exist, and the following line is added to it:
options(radian.auto_match = FALSE)
The ~/.lintr file is also created if it does not exist, and the following lines are added to it:
linters: linters_with_defaults(
    object_length_linter = NULL,
    object_name_linter = NULL)
